newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's Suzuken, Akiyama say to merge in April '98.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Suzuken, Akiyama say to merge in April '98.

text.p: Japanese prescription drug wholesaler Suzuken Co Ltd and pharmaceutical wholesaler Akiyama Inc said on Thursday that they plan to merge on April 1, 1998.
In the merger, one Akiyama share will be exchanged for 0.32 of a Suzuken share, the two firms said in a joint statement. Akiyama will be dissolved as a result of the merger, they said.
The two firms, both of which are listed on the second section of the Tokyo bourse, have had a business-and-equity tie-up since February 1994.
Suzuken is based in Nagoya in central Japan, while Akiyama is based in Sapporo, the largest city on Japan's northernmost main island of Hokkaido.
The merged company will be capitalised at 13.11 billion yen with total assets worth 479 billion yen, the two firms said.
They said the new company was expected to post a current profit of 20.26 billion yen in the financial year to March 1999, and 22.50 billion yen the following year.
